scenes.headline: How one token sequence teaches robot hands
scenes.sub: Natura-1 learns dexterity from human video
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mitten! Here's how Nature Will's new robot model turns human video into moves for robot hands.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: A whole episode of language, images, video and actions becomes one causal sequence, and future video and actions are denoised together.
scenes.say: The idea: put a whole episode into one sequence, and predict the future video and the actions together.

steps.say: First come the instruction and the video seen so far. The past is kept as memory.
Noise fills the future slots. One mixture of experts transformer reads the whole stream, left to right.

steps.note: separate losses for video and action
steps.say: Flow matching denoises future video and hand actions together, each with its own loss.
Video is abundant, so predicting it gives far more signal than actions alone.

steps.label: stated
steps.say: Attention is causal. Each step sees every earlier step, never a later one. So one pass trains a prediction at every step.

scenes.title: From human video to robot hands

items.say: It starts with a million hours of first person human video.
An in house tool reconstructs hand and body motion. Those poses become the actions.
Captions describe goals down to single steps, so a different instruction means a different future.
Then a small amount of robot data adapts it to dexterous robot hands.

steps.say: On robot data it never trained on, action error falls about two thirds as training reaches a million hours.
But it is teacher forced prediction error, along what looks like one run. Not task success.

scenes.title: Benchmark, two different robots
scenes.note: baselines scored nothing on the hands
scenes.say: On an in house benchmark it scores fifty three point four. The baselines scored nothing on hands, so their numbers come from a gripper robot.

scenes.text: Put the whole episode in one sequence and video carries most of the learning.
scenes.say: One sequence per episode, and video carries most of the learning. The numbers still need an outside check.

recap: Human video first, robot data last
scenes.say: One sequence per episode. Video and actions denoised together. Human video first, robot data last.
